title: FESTIval: A versatile framework for conducting experimental evaluations of spatial indices
author: Carniel, Ciferri, et al.

steps.title: Configure experimental parameters
steps.instruction: Set up the experiment using the Brazil buildings dataset (src_id = brazil_buildings2017) containing 1,485,866 regions. Use a Kingston SSD V300 (480 GB) as storage. Configure each index with an in‑memory buffer of 512 KB, a log size of 10 MB, and a flushing unit size of 5. Do not use a generic buffer (buf_id = 1). Assign specialized‑configuration IDs: sc_id = 50031 for the eFIND R‑tree and sc_id = 1323 for the FAST R‑tree. Vary the basic‑configuration ID (bc_id) to test page sizes from 2 KB to 32 KB (e.g., bc_id = 53 corresponds to a 4 KB page size). Apply the best‑known values for all other parameters.

steps.title: Execute workload for 4 KB page size
steps.instruction: Run the FESTIval workload for each index with page size 4 KB (bc_id = 53) and store the results on the HDD:

steps.title: Repeat workload across page sizes
steps.instruction: For each additional page size (bc_id values covering 2 KB–32 KB), issue the corresponding FT_QueryWorkload SELECT statement five times, changing the index file name each run to obtain five independent executions. After each execution, clear the PostgreSQL cache and the operating‑system cache before the next run.

steps.title: Compute eFIND index statistics
steps.instruction: Query the FESTIval schema to obtain the average index‑construction time and its standard deviation for the eFIND R‑tree at each page size:

substeps.instruction:
SELECT b.page_size, avg(e.index_time), stddev(e.index_time)
FROM fds.basicconfiguration b, fds.specializedconfiguration sc, fds.indexconfiguration ic, fds.spatialindex si, fds.execution e
WHERE b.bc_id = ic.bc_id AND sc.sc_id = ic.sc_id AND ic.config_id = si.config_id AND si.idx_id = e.idx_id AND ic.sc_id = 50031 AND execution_name = 'Query Worload - Index Creation'
GROUP BY b.page_size
ORDER BY b.page_size;

steps.title: Compute FAST index statistics
steps.instruction: Run the same query as above, replacing the specialized‑configuration ID with the FAST value (sc_id = 1323) to obtain statistics for the FAST R‑tree:

substeps.instruction:
SELECT b.page_size, avg(e.index_time), stddev(e.index_time)
FROM fds.basicconfiguration b, fds.specializedconfiguration sc, fds.indexconfiguration ic, fds.spatialindex si, fds.execution e
WHERE b.bc_id = ic.bc_id AND sc.sc_id = ic.sc_id AND ic.config_id = si.config_id AND si.idx_id = e.idx_id AND ic.sc_id = 1323 AND execution_name = 'Query Worload - Index Creation'
GROUP BY b.page_size
ORDER BY b.page_size;

steps.title: Compute IRQ execution statistics
steps.instruction: For each page size, calculate the average total elapsed time of the 100 IRQs with query windows covering 0.001 % of Brazil’s area:

substeps.instruction:
SELECT t.page_size, avg(t.s), stddev(t.s)
FROM (
  SELECT si.idx_name, b.page_size, sum(e.index_time) as s
  FROM fds.basicconfiguration b, fds.specializedconfiguration sc, fds.indexconfiguration ic, fds.spatialindex si, fds.execution e
  WHERE b.bc_id = ic.bc_id AND sc.sc_id = ic.sc_id AND ic.config_id = si.config_id AND si.idx_id = e.idx_id AND ic.sc_id = 50031 AND execution_name = 'Query Worload - Execution of IRQs with Query Windows of 0.001'
  GROUP BY si.idx_name, b.page_size
) as t
GROUP BY t.page_size
ORDER BY t.page_size;

steps.title: Visualize performance results
steps.instruction: Import the result tables (page_size, average time, standard deviation) into a data‑analytics tool and create bar graphs where the x‑axis is page_size and the y‑axis is the average time with error bars representing the standard deviation.
